11.0 THE COMMANDS TABLE AND THE SCREENS

11.1 Three levels, fixed places

FS 6.13. The level of a command is what it acts on. Each level has one place, the same on every tab, so the owner, after a month away, has one rule to remember.

[[FIG screen_layout | The screen: where each level of command lives]]
DR-11.1The menus (global strip, Commands button panel, caption "v" menu, a layer's chip menu) shall be built from the commands table by filtering on scope and on the context (active tab, subtab, layer). No screen shall build a menu item by hand.
DR-11.2Context-aware commands: one save, saveAs, export, reset, help, notes, history each, reading the context to decide what they act on. A tab supplies a small adapter (what "the open item" is), not its own command.
DR-11.3Keyboard: each command may declare a key; keys are shown in the menus; the same key does the same kind of thing on every tab (Ctrl+S save, Ctrl+Z undo, Delete delete the selection).
DR-11.4Before the table is written, a survey of every V1 command shall be made (FR-6.13.7): id, label, where it is now, which level it belongs to, and duplicates. The survey is reviewed by the owner.

11.2 Acceptance tests

AT-11.1On every tab, Help is in the same place and opens the page for that tab and subtab.
AT-11.2Save on Draw, Figures and Patterns is one command id; its greyed tooltip, with nothing open, says "nothing open to save".
AT-11.3A code search finds no menu item built outside screens/menus.js.

12.0 ERROR HANDLING

FS 6.14. The design rule: no checks in the logic; catch at a few choke points; show every error; never stop the whole application (D-12). V1 has this since claude/v1-errors; V2 is built with it.

Choke pointOn error
A layer's evaluationThat layer draws nothing and shows a red mark; the others draw. The error names the document and layer.
A command's runThe document is unchanged (DR-7.4); the error names the command.
A tab switchThe tab shows a message in its main area; other tabs work.
Reading or writing a fileThe item is marked; the error names the file and what was wrong with it.
Registering a generator, template or connectorIt is listed greyed with the reason; others load.
A script run (in its frame)The frame reports it; the script's view shows it; the app is unaffected.
Anything uncaughtThe window's error and unhandled-rejection handlers report it as "uncaught".
ErrorRecord   = { time, where, message, place, count }     // place: "file:line" of the owner's code, if any
error log     = journal/logs/errors_YYYY-MM-DD.txt, one line per new error:
  2026-11-02 14:03:11  Figure "star", layer 3 (parabola): steps is not a number  (generators/parabola.js:22)
DR-12.1The error bar is a fixed region of the page, on every tab, not cleared by a tab switch; it lists the latest five different errors with counts, and a Dismiss.
DR-12.2An error is logged once per page load per (where, message); repeats increment the count shown in the bar.
DR-12.3An error inside the error handler itself is written only to the console, so a fault in reporting cannot loop.
DR-12.4At start-up, Home summarises the newest error log (count and latest lines) with its own Dismiss, remembered by file name and count, so new errors in the same file show again.
DR-12.5Debug checks (FR-6.14.5) are in documents/checks.js, run after each command when session.debug is on: point numbers unique and below nextPoint; every handle names an existing point; every attached point names an existing layer; order lists every layer once. A failure is reported like any error.

12.1 Acceptance tests

AT-12.1Make one layer's generator throw: the bar names the layer; the other layers draw; the log has one line; redraw ten times: the count is 11, the log still one line.
AT-12.2Reload: Home says the newest error log has 1 error.

13.0 EXPLORATION GENERATORS AND GEOMETRY ALGORITHMS

13.1 Lattice with shared points

The manyRowsColumns model (FR-6.19.1): M shapes per row, N rows, neighbours sharing points, so one drag reshapes several shapes. Copies are added with a setting.

lattice(settings):
  shape: a generator id with k handles; rows N, cols M; spacing dx, dy; shareRule: "edges" | "corners" | "none"
  lay out an (M+1) x (N+1) grid of point numbers in the document's point table (created once, kept on resize
    where positions exist, new ones added at the grid position)
  for each cell (r, c): a child layer of the shape whose handles name the grid's point numbers for that cell,
    chosen by shareRule (corners: the four cell corners; edges: also the edge mid-points)
  the lattice is one layer to the owner (one settings panel), many layers to evaluation
DR-13.1Changing M or N keeps every existing point where it was dragged; new points take grid positions (manyRowsColumns re-seeds and loses drags; V2 shall not).
DR-13.2A lattice may list several shapes, used in a repeating pattern across the cells, and an overlay layer (one shape resting on top, its own colour) (FR-6.19.2).
DR-13.3A drag of a shared point is one command and redraws every cell using it in the same frame (DR-6.6).

13.2 Symmetry repeat

Any layer may carry repeat: { n, center, mirror }: evaluated once, drawn n times turned 360/n° about the centre (and mirrored if asked). Repeated copies are drawn, not new layers; their nails are real (they print) and numbered after the original's.

13.3 Component groups

A group file lists layers with mostly default settings and their welds; inserting it inserts them all, as one command, with fresh point numbers (FR-6.19.5).

13.4 Roulettes

roulette(R, r, d, turns, steps, dChange):
  k = (R - r) / r
  for i in 0..steps: th = turns * 2pi * i / steps;  dd = d + dChange * th / (2pi)
    x = (R - r) cos th + dd cos(k th);  y = (R - r) sin th - dd sin(k th)
  closes after turns = r / gcd(R, r) when R and r are whole numbers; otherwise never: limited by turns

13.5 Templates

FS 6.20. A template is a generator with meta.kind = "template", inserted with role guide: shown while working, left out of Show All, Final and output. The first set: rectangle, circle, ruler (shows its length in the caption, in mm once the scale is set), bounding box of the figure, saw tooth, grid.

13.6 The pursuit engine

One engine for every V1 pursuit script (FR-6.19.6). Prototype: gallery/Ideabook/scripts/pursuitEngine.js.

pursuitSteps(start: Point[], s):
  defaults: steps 40, rule "next", k 2, move "fraction", f 0.08, speed 4, speeds null,
            bias 0, jitter 0, seed 1, reverse false, center, radius 100, target
  pts = reverse ? start reversed : start;  rnd = seeded(seed);  heading = none for each point
  out = [pts]
  repeat steps times:
    for each point p_i:
      t = target by rule:  next p_(i+1) | kth p_(i+k) | opposite p_(i+n/2) | centroid of all
                           | random (a target fixed per point from rnd) | circle (a point moving on a circle)
                           | fixed (s.target) | a function (i, pts, step)
      d = t - p_i
      rate = speeds ? speeds[i] : (move = "speed" ? speed : f)
      d = move = "speed" ? unit(d) * min(rate, |d|) : d * rate
      d = d * (1 - bias) + heading_i * bias;   heading_i = d
      p_i' = p_i + d + jitter * (rnd() - 0.5) * 2 (each axis)
    pts = all p'; out.push(pts)
  return out                                    // drawn as "edges" (nested polygons) or "trails" (each point's path)
V1 script (gallery/Scripts/Pursuit/)Engine settings that reproduce it
pursuit.jsrule next, move fraction, cw or ccw by reverse; as edges
pursuitMice.jsthe same, start a regular n-gon
pursuit2.jsrule next | kth | centroid; speeds from a seed for its "speeds" rule
pursuit3.jsrule next, as trails
pursuitStatic5 / Dynamic5.jsseveral runs, some reversed
copilot1 / copilotAnimation.jsmove speed, bias, jitter, rule random | opposite | circle | fixed; animation = drawing steps over time
pusuitSurface.jsnot covered: it fills polygons (playpen)
pursuit4.jsnot a pursuit: a stitch rule (pairwise with offset 2 sides)

13.7 Intersections

Intersections are nail candidates, shown with their own mark, distinct from magic points (FR-6.2.7a, 6.21).

intersections(pathA, pathB, s):
  segments of A and B (a closed path includes its closing segment)
  candidate pairs by a uniform grid of cell size = 2 x the mean segment length (avoids n*m)
  for each pair, solve the two-segment intersection; keep 0 <= u, v <= 1
  merge points closer than 0.5 px
  name each "cross A.B #k", k numbered by angle about the pair's joint centroid from straight up, clockwise (DR-4.9)
tracking: a disc attached to "cross A.B #k" is re-found after a change by name; if #k no longer exists,
  the nearest crossing to its last position within 5 px is taken and the change noted; otherwise it is marked lost (DR-6.3)
DR-13.4Self-intersections only on request (DR-4.11). At most 400 intersections per pair are offered (V1's cap), the rest counted.
DR-13.5Later (FR-6.21.2), an intersection may be defined by rule: "the k-th crossing of A and B counted from A's start", which is stable where angle numbering is not.
DR-13.6The owner's own intersection routine shall be studied first: for which curves it works and why it fails on others, and kept if it is better on its curves.

13.8 Image to thread (later)

FR-6.19.7, for analysis now, building later: approximate a photograph with one continuous thread across N nails on a circle. The known greedy method: start at a nail; repeatedly choose the next nail whose straight line most darkens the remaining darkness of the image along it; subtract the line; stop after L lines or when no line helps. Output is a nail sequence, the build instructions in this one case.

13.9 Acceptance tests

AT-13.1A 3 × 2 lattice of Parabolas sharing corners: drag a shared corner, all cells using it follow; change to 4 × 2: the dragged corner stays.
AT-13.2Each V1 pursuit script listed as covered is reproduced by the engine within 1 px per point for its default settings.
AT-13.3Two crossing lines give one intersection named "cross L1.line.L2.line #1"; a disc on it follows as one line turns 10°.
